items.title: Tony Fougerat Interview, 1960-06-08
items.q: A man like Hardy and Rene and Sam Morgan and... Buck Johnson, King Oliver. All them fellas had a different style.

ctx.x: Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm.

Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. well they called them cafes in them days, on Rampart Street. Him and King Oliver was playing together. Loey was playing the second trumpet. I never will forget that. And I was just starting out and I heard so much about Loey. And I went in there and heard him playing. And then in later years after he got playing good there, there was a little boy come up there by the name of Emmett Harding. He was very…
You talked about Rene, and you were saying how good he was.
